title: Signal Cartographer: tune SLO-trigger thresholds and hysteresis for canary rollouts
creator: Marco Liu
description: Problem: Current canary rollback triggers are brittle across workloads. Simple fixed thresholds for latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput cause noisy rollbacks when traffic composition shifts (short vs long queries, bursty vs steady). We need a systematic way to map multi-signal SLOs to adaptive thresholds with cohort-aware hysteresis so canaries fail open/closed appropriately and avoid unnecessary rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a prototype agent (signal cartographer) that ingests P50/P95 latency, 5xx error rate, token_cost_per_request, and qps, and outputs a recommended threshold set for canary triggers.
Recommendations include: baseline threshold, short/long-query cohort adjustments, and hysteresis window values for each signal.

Automated simulation harness that replays historical traffic (3 production traces) and demonstrates >= 35% reduction in false-positive rollbacks vs current fixed-threshold baseline while maintaining >= 95% detection of real regressions injected in tests.
Design doc + config schema for integrating recommendations into rollout policies and UI controls in the Console.
Unit tests and end-to-end integration test in staging: canary deploys with recommended thresholds must behave deterministically (no flapping) for two synthetic burst scenarios.
Feature flag gating and rollout plan documented for Dedicated and Hosted customers.
design_notes: Use Bayesian change-point detection to estimate drift in latency/error signals and produce conservative posterior intervals as threshold candidates.
Cohorting: derive cohorts by request token length buckets (<=64, 65-512, >512) and by traffic percentile (steady vs burst). Adjust thresholds per cohort using quantile-normalized deltas.
Hysteresis: recommend separate enter/exit windows (e.g., 5min enter, 10min exit) per signal to avoid oscillation; tune via simulation grid search on historical traces.
Cost signal: token_cost is noisy for short requests; apply EWMA smoothing and couple with throughput to compute a normalized per-token SLO contribution.
Fallbacks: if signals are missing or low volume, default to conservative fixed thresholds defined in rollout policy; log telemetry for offline tuning.
Exposed knobs for PMs in Console: aggressiveness (beta|balanced|conservative), cohort scope override, and manual hysteresis overrides.
Privacy: all telemetry uses aggregated counts and pre-aggregation filters; no user content leaves VPC in Private deployments.
tasks: Prototype signal cartographer library (python) to compute thresholds from input time-series
Build simulation harness that replays three production traces with injected regressions
Create config schema and API endpoint for serving recommendations
Integrate recommendations into canary controller (server-side) behind a feature flag
Instrument Console UI to present recommended thresholds and allow manual accept/reject
Run staging A/B: new tuner vs baseline across 2 workload classes and collect metrics
Document rollout plan and update runbook with diagnostics for tuned thresholds
